doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Army, politics and jazz in Cuba
title: Army band and finishing the conservatory in uniform
summary: In the army concert band with strong young players, he continued clarinet studies and gave his graduation recital dressed as a soldier.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: While you were in the army, were you able to play music at all?

Yes because in the army, I was in the marching band. They have a concert band, in the army. Pretty good, pretty good, because they have many of the young musicians in the streets, in the cabarets and in the symphony and all that, and they put it together a pretty good concert band.
And, were there other musicians in that army band that later became professional musicians?
Many of them; not a lot of people, but yea; some of those kids were first line in the conservatory in those days.
And, while you were in the army, were you able to continue your studies?

Yes, I finish my studies in the conservatory while in the army. I got waited in the Havana Conservatory, while in the army. In 1966, around there, I was able to go to the conservatory two or three times a week to study, to fit in my clarinet studies. Actually, I did my recital, my graduating recital in the conservatory, dressed as a soldier, because in those days, I have a service and I have only to wear fatigues.
